anti_overlap: Do not critique normative MUST/SHOULD language — that is the RFC editor's concern
Do not assess voice/register portability — that is the TTRPG designer's concern
Stay out of cross-repo governance and amendment workflows
decision_lens: When the write-revel-proposal skill and UB's equivalent skill both emit Proposal artifacts, will a downstream eval/replay/debug tool be able to consume both without per-game branching?
distance_rationale: Parallel discipline: both define a shared output schema that multiple LLM-driven agents must conform to while preserving distinct voice/register, but in general AI-skill engineering rather than culture-sim game design specifically.
expected_isomorphisms: The 'shared output contract + per-skill prompt template' pattern in agent-skill engineering maps directly to 'shared Proposal/Debrief schema + per-game advisor prompt'. Evaluation, replay, and debugging requirements for LLM artifacts transfer wholesale — the spec is consumed not just by humans but by tools (eval, replay) the brainstorm explicitly mentions.
focus: Whether the shared schemas survive contact with two divergent LLM-driven advisor agents and remain machine-tractable for downstream tooling
name: fd-llm-multi-agent-prompt-template-contract
persona: Apply the perspective of an LLM agent-skill engineer who has shipped multiple skills sharing one output contract — they care about whether two independently prompted LLMs can reliably produce schema-conformant artifacts, measure success by parse-failure rate and downstream tool compatibility, and flag any field where natural-language ambiguity will cause the model to drift.
review_areas: Field tractability: can an LLM reliably produce each required field given only the prompt + spec, without per-game fine-tuning?
Free-text fields: are 'summary', 'rationale', 'lessons' bounded (length, structure) or unbounded prose that will defy parsing?
event_local_name handling: is it an enum, a free string, or a registry? Will downstream tools need to know all valid values?
Annotation embedding: how do annotation verbs round-trip through the artifact when Annotate-stage output feeds the next Prepare stage?
Failure modes: what should the advisor emit when it cannot fill a required field? Is there a defined null/unknown convention?
Replay/eval compatibility: can a debugging tool consume both games' artifacts with a single parser, or is per-game branching required?

severity_examples.condition: summary/rationale/lessons defined without max length, format hint, or schema validation
severity_examples.scenario: Required field is unbounded free prose with no length cap or structure

severity_examples.condition: Field accepts arbitrary strings with no enumeration mechanism for downstream tools
severity_examples.scenario: event_local_name is open-ended with no registry

severity_examples.condition: Spec does not specify how Annotate-stage output is encoded back into next-cycle Proposal inputs
Spec does not state what an advisor emits when it cannot generate a confident rationale

source_domain: LLM prompt-template engineering for multi-agent skill systems (shared schema, agent/game-specific content; multi-skill contract design across products)
success_hints: Treat each schema field as a prompt-engineering target
Identify which fields require structured output mode vs free completion
Propose a minimum eval-tool compatibility test
task_context: Reviewing shared JSON schemas that will be produced by two independently prompted LLM advisor agents (Hermes-as-Curator, Hermes-as-Steward) and consumed by cross-product debugging/eval tooling.
